question: How appealing is this offer to you personally? Answer with a single whole number from 1 (not at all appealing) to 10 (extremely appealing).

concepts.text: Earn 4.25% APY on your savings with no monthly fees and no minimum balance.

variants.plain: Get a 4.25% yearly return, counting interest on your interest, on your savings, with no monthly charges and no smallest amount you have to keep in the account.
variants.alt: Grow your savings at 4.25% APY, with zero monthly fees and no minimum balance required.
variants.frame_flip: Don't miss out on 4.25% APY on your savings, and stop losing money to monthly fees and minimum balance rules.
variants.reordered: No minimum balance, no monthly fees, and 4.25% APY on your savings.

plain.reason: Explains APY as yearly return with compounding; same rate, no monthly fees, no minimum balance.

alt.reason: Same rate, no monthly fees, no minimum balance; only wording changed.

frame_flip.reason: Loss-framed tone, but the facts are the same: 4.25% APY, no monthly fees, no minimum balance.

reordered.reason: Same three facts in a different order.

concepts.text: Put your spare change to work: every card purchase rounds up and the difference goes into your savings.

variants.plain: Make your leftover cents useful: each time you pay with your card, the amount is rounded up and the extra is added to your savings.
variants.alt: Let your loose change grow: we round up every card purchase and move the extra into your savings.
variants.frame_flip: Stop letting your spare change go to waste: every card purchase rounds up so the difference lands in your savings instead of slipping away.
variants.reordered: Your savings get the difference every time a card purchase rounds up, putting your spare change to work.

plain.reason: Same mechanism: every card purchase rounded up, difference to savings.

alt.reason: Same round-up on every card purchase with extra moved to savings; 'grow' is tone, not a new promise of interest.

frame_flip.reason: Loss framing only; same facts and conditions.

reordered.reason: Same content reordered; every card purchase rounds up and difference goes to savings.

concepts.text: Stop losing money to overdraft fees. Our account never charges you $35 for going $5 over.

variants.plain: Quit wasting money on fees for spending more than you have. With our account, you'll never pay $35 just because you went $5 below zero.
variants.alt: Say goodbye to costly overdraft fees. Go $5 over with our account and you'll never get hit with a $35 charge.
variants.reordered: Our account never charges you $35 for going $5 over. So you can stop losing money to overdraft fees.

plain.reason: Restates overdraft fees in plain words; same $35 fee and $5 overdraft, same promise.

alt.reason: Same promise: no $35 charge for going $5 over. Only the wording and tone changed.

frame_flip.reason: Adds new claims ('every month', 'other banks would charge you') and frames the promise as keeping $35, which shifts the offer beyond the original no-fee statement.

reordered.reason: Same sentences in a different order; facts and promise unchanged.

concepts.text: Get 2% cash back on every purchase, 3% on groceries, and 5% on travel booked through our portal, up to $1,500 per quarter.

variants.plain: Earn 2% of your money back on everything you buy, 3% back on groceries, and 5% back on trips you book through our website, up to $1,500 every three months.
variants.frame_flip: Don't miss out on 2% cash back on every purchase, 3% on groceries, and 5% on travel booked through our portal, up to $1,500 per quarter you'd otherwise leave on the table.
variants.reordered: Up to $1,500 per quarter: 5% cash back on travel booked through our portal, 3% on groceries, and 2% on every other purchase.

plain.reason: Same rates, categories, portal condition, and $1,500 cap; 'every three months' equals per quarter.

alt.reason: It says the cap is '$1,500 in rewards' each quarter. The original's '$1,500 per quarter' does not say whether the cap applies to rewards or to spending, so the rewrite narrows a condition.

frame_flip.reason: Only the loss-aversion framing is added; all rates, conditions, and the cap are unchanged.

reordered.reason: Same rates, categories, portal condition, and quarterly cap. 'Every other purchase' only makes explicit the usual non-stacking reading of the base 2% rate.

concepts.text: A savings account that grows with you. Set a goal, and we'll help you reach it.

variants.plain: A savings account that gets bigger as your life changes. Pick something to save for, and we'll help you get there.
variants.reordered: Set a goal, and we'll help you reach it, with a savings account that grows with you.

plain.reason: Same account, same goal-setting help; 'gets bigger as your life changes' paraphrases 'grows with you'.

alt.reason: 'Support you all the way to it' strengthens 'help you reach it' into an implied promise of seeing the goal through. Dropping 'account' also blurs what the product is.

frame_flip.reason: 'Make sure you don't fall short' turns help into something close to a guarantee. 'Won't leave you behind' does not mean the account grows.

reordered.reason: Same claims and promise, only reordered.

concepts.text: Our card's variable APR of 19.99% is lower than the national average, and there's no annual fee.

variants.plain: Our card's yearly interest rate is 19.99% and can change over time. That's lower than the average across the country, and you won't pay a fee each year to have the card.
variants.alt: With a variable APR of just 19.99%, below the national average, and no annual fee, our card keeps more money in your pocket.
variants.reordered: There's no annual fee on our card, and its variable APR of 19.99% is lower than the national average.

plain.reason: Explains variable APR as a yearly rate that can change, keeps 19.99%, below national average, and no annual fee. Same facts.

alt.reason: Same rate, comparison and no annual fee. 'Keeps more money in your pocket' is promotional framing, not a new fact or condition.

frame_flip.reason: 'Saves you from the higher national average' implies guaranteed savings, which the original does not promise. 'Never' adds a permanence promise about the annual fee that the original does not make.

reordered.reason: Only the order of the clauses changed. All facts and numbers are unchanged.

concepts.text: Open an account today and get a $200 bonus. Limited time only.

variants.plain: Sign up for an account today and you'll get a $200 bonus. This offer won't last long.
variants.alt: Start your account today and pick up a $200 bonus. For a limited time only.
variants.frame_flip: Don't miss out on a $200 bonus: open an account today. Limited time only.
variants.reordered: For a limited time only: get a $200 bonus when you open an account today.

plain.reason: Same action (open/sign up for account today), same $200 bonus, and 'won't last long' conveys limited time.

alt.reason: 'Start your account' equals opening one; $200 bonus and limited-time condition preserved.

frame_flip.reason: Loss-framed wording only; account opening today, $200 bonus, and limited time all retained.

reordered.reason: Same facts reordered; the 'when you open' conditional matches the original's implied condition.

concepts.text: Your deposits are FDIC-insured up to $250,000, so your money is safe with us.

variants.plain: The Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation, a U.S. government agency, insures the money you keep with us up to $250,000, so your money is safe with us.
variants.alt: With FDIC insurance covering your deposits up to $250,000, you can count on your money being safe with us.
variants.frame_flip: Your deposits are FDIC-insured up to $250,000, so you gain the confidence of knowing your money is protected with us.
variants.reordered: Your money is safe with us, because your deposits are FDIC-insured up to $250,000.

plain.reason: Spells out FDIC as a U.S. government agency, which is an accurate expansion rather than a new fact. Same $250,000 limit and same safety claim.

alt.reason: Same FDIC coverage, same $250,000 limit and same safety promise, reworded.

frame_flip.reason: Recasts 'safe' as 'protected' with a confidence framing. Facts and limit are unchanged.

reordered.reason: Same clauses in reverse order, with the causal link preserved.

concepts.text: High-yield savings at 4.10% APY, compounded daily, with zero fees.

variants.plain: A savings account that pays 4.10% interest a year (annual percentage yield), with interest added every day, and no fees at all.
variants.alt: Grow your savings at 4.10% APY, with interest compounding every day and absolutely no fees.
variants.frame_flip: Stop missing out on 4.10% APY: daily compounding and zero fees mean none of your savings' growth gets left behind.
variants.reordered: Zero fees, interest compounded daily, and a high-yield savings rate of 4.10% APY.

plain.reason: Same rate (4.10% APY), daily compounding, no fees. It drops the 'high-yield' label, but that is descriptive, not a fact.

alt.reason: Same 4.10% APY, daily compounding and zero fees. Only the tone changed.

frame_flip.reason: Loss-aversion framing, but the facts are unchanged: 4.10% APY, daily compounding, zero fees. 'None of your savings' growth gets left behind' is rhetorical, not a new condition.

reordered.reason: Same elements in a different order.

concepts.text: Get paid up to two days early with direct deposit.

variants.plain: Set up direct deposit and your paycheck can land in your account as much as two days sooner.
variants.alt: Your paycheck, up to two days sooner, when you choose direct deposit.
variants.frame_flip: Stop waiting up to two extra days for your pay: use direct deposit.
variants.reordered: With direct deposit, get paid up to two days early.

plain.reason: Keeps direct deposit as the condition and 'as much as two days sooner' as the ceiling. 'Can land' preserves the hedge of 'up to'.

alt.reason: Same condition (direct deposit) and same 'up to two days' ceiling. Only the order of the parts changed.

frame_flip.reason: Recasts early pay as avoiding a wait of up to two days. The amount, the hedge and the direct-deposit condition all stay the same.

reordered.reason: Same words in a different order. No facts were added or dropped.

concepts.text: Don't let inflation eat your savings. Move your money to an account that keeps up.

variants.plain: Don't let rising prices shrink what you've saved. Put your money in an account that grows as fast as prices go up.
variants.alt: Stop watching inflation chip away at your savings. Switch to an account that keeps pace.
variants.frame_flip: Help your savings hold their full value. Move your money to an account that keeps up with inflation.
variants.reordered: Move your money to an account that keeps up, and don't let inflation eat your savings.

plain.reason: Rising prices = inflation; 'grows as fast as prices go up' restates 'keeps up'. No facts added or dropped.

alt.reason: Same promise with different wording: 'keeps pace' = 'keeps up', and 'switch' = 'move'.

frame_flip.reason: Positive framing of the same promise. 'Keeps up with inflation' only makes explicit what the original implied.

reordered.reason: Same two statements in a different order. Nothing added or removed.

concepts.text: Earn 1.5 points per dollar, 3x points on dining, 4x on streaming, and a 60,000-point welcome bonus after you spend $4,000 in 3 months.

variants.plain: Get 1.5 points for every dollar you spend, 3 times the points when you eat out, 4 times the points on streaming services, plus 60,000 extra points once you spend $4,000 within your first 3 months.
variants.alt: Rack up 1.5 points on every dollar, triple points at restaurants, quadruple points on streaming, and unlock a 60,000-point welcome bonus when you spend $4,000 in your first 3 months.
variants.frame_flip: Don't miss out on 1.5 points per dollar, 3x points on dining, 4x on streaming, or the 60,000-point welcome bonus you'd forfeit without spending $4,000 in 3 months.
variants.reordered: Spend $4,000 in 3 months to get a 60,000-point welcome bonus, plus 4x points on streaming, 3x on dining, and 1.5 points per dollar on everything else.

plain.reason: All rates (1.5x base, 3x dining, 4x streaming), the 60,000-point bonus, and the $4,000-in-3-months condition are preserved. 'Within your first 3 months' is a faithful reading of 'in 3 months'.

alt.reason: 'Triple' and 'quadruple' equal 3x and 4x, and 'restaurants' is a reasonable stand-in for dining. The bonus amount and spend condition are unchanged.

frame_flip.reason: This is a loss-framed restatement. The forfeit clause applies only to the welcome bonus, which matches the original condition, and all numbers are unchanged.

reordered.reason: Only the order changes. 'On everything else' just makes explicit that 1.5x is the base rate for other purchases, and all numbers and conditions are intact.

concepts.text: See all your accounts in one place and know exactly where your money goes.

variants.alt: Bring every account together in a single view and get a clear picture of where each dollar ends up.
variants.frame_flip: Stop jumping between accounts and stop losing track of where your money goes, with everything in one place.
variants.reordered: Know exactly where your money goes by seeing all your accounts in one place.

plain.reason: Narrows 'all your accounts' to 'bank accounts' and adds 'on one screen'; 'what you spend on' is close but the account scope changed.

alt.reason: Same promise: all accounts in one view and a clear understanding of where money goes. 'Clear picture' is a minor softening of 'exactly' but acceptable wording.

frame_flip.reason: Negative framing of the same two benefits: everything in one place and knowing where money goes. No facts added or dropped.

reordered.reason: Same facts, only the clause order is changed.

concepts.text: No foreign transaction fees and no annual fee, ever.

variants.plain: You never pay extra charges for buying things in other countries, and you never pay a yearly fee for the card.
variants.alt: Zero fees on purchases abroad and zero annual fee, for good.
variants.reordered: No annual fee, ever, and no foreign transaction fees.

plain.reason: Restates both promises, no foreign transaction fees and no annual fee, with 'never' preserving 'ever.' The wording is plainer, but the facts are unchanged.

alt.reason: 'Zero fees on purchases abroad' corresponds to no foreign transaction fees, and 'for good' matches 'ever.' No facts are added or dropped.

frame_flip.reason: 'Keep every dollar you spend abroad' overstates the promise. It suggests no cost of any kind abroad (e.g., no exchange-rate markup) rather than just no foreign transaction fees. 'Keep your card free' is also vaguer than 'no annual fee.'

reordered.reason: Same two promises, only reordered. 'Ever' attached to the annual fee still reads as applying to the whole offer.

concepts.text: Act now: lock in a 12-month CD at 4.5% APY before rates drop.

variants.plain: Don't wait: get a 12-month savings certificate earning 4.5% a year before interest rates go down.
variants.alt: Hurry and secure 4.5% APY on a 12-month CD while today's rates last.
variants.reordered: Before rates drop, lock in 4.5% APY on a 12-month CD—act now.

plain.reason: Same 12-month term, 4.5% annual yield, and urgency before rates fall; 'savings certificate' and '4.5% a year' are plain-language equivalents of CD and APY.

alt.reason: Same rate and term. 'While today's rates last' carries the same implied rate-drop urgency.

frame_flip.reason: Drops the claim that rates will drop. Adds the subjective 'solid' and the new condition 'today'.

reordered.reason: Same elements in a different order: rates dropping, lock in 4.5% APY, 12-month CD, act now.

concepts.text: Free financial coaching for every member, whenever you need it.

variants.plain: Every member can get free help with money planning from a coach, any time they need it.
variants.frame_flip: Never face money worries alone: every member gets free financial coaching, whenever you need it.
variants.reordered: Whenever you need it, every member gets financial coaching, free.

plain.reason: Same offer: free coaching for every member, any time needed. 'Help with money planning' is a fair paraphrase of financial coaching.

alt.reason: Adds 'expert', a claim about coach qualifications that is not in the original. 'Whenever it suits you' is acceptable wording, but 'expert' changes the promise.

frame_flip.reason: Only adds an emotional framing line. The facts are unchanged: free coaching for every member, whenever needed.

reordered.reason: Same facts in a different order: free financial coaching for every member, whenever needed.

rules_after_batch1.definition: uses financial jargon or acronyms (APY, APR, FDIC, CD, compounding, variable rate, yield)
sells by saying what is NOT there (no fees, never, zero, without, don't)
frames the offer as avoiding a loss (stop losing, don't let X eat, miss out, before it's gone)
contains three or more separate numbers or percentages

rules_after_batch1.rule: On a synthetic AI panel, copy over ~22 words scored 0.42 points lower on a 1-10 appeal scale (90% CI -0.73 to -0.08; 7 variants, 5 concepts); fragile finding.
rules_after_batch1.advice: Lean toward keeping copy under about 22 words. Treat this as a tentative signal, since the evidence is fragile and comes from AI personas. Check it with real audiences before making it a firm rule.

rules_after_batch1.definition: pressures the reader on time (today, now, limited time, act now, before rates drop)

rules_final.definition: uses financial jargon or acronyms (APY, APR, FDIC, CD, compounding, variable rate, yield)
sells by saying what is NOT there (no fees, never, zero, without, don't)
frames the offer as avoiding a loss (stop losing, don't let X eat, miss out, before it's gone)
contains three or more separate numbers or percentages

rules_final.rule: On a synthetic AI-persona panel, concepts longer than about 22 words scored 0.4 points lower on 1-10 appeal (90% CI -0.65 to -0.1; 9 variants, 7 concepts); fragile finding.
rules_final.advice: Consider trimming copy to about 22 words or fewer, but treat this as a tentative signal from AI personas and confirm with real-audience testing before making it a rule.

rules_final.definition: pressures the reader on time (today, now, limited time, act now, before rates drop)
